docs.title: About
docs.text:
Dr. Hai-Tao Yu is a Tenured Associate Professor at University of Tsukuba, Japan, leading the Information Intelligence research group. His research currently focuses Retrieval-augmented LLM, Trustworthy Information Retrieval and Commonsense Reasoning. He has published a series of papers on top international conferences (e.g., WSDM, CIKM, SIGIR, WWW, ECIR, and AAAI) and journals (e.g., Information Processing and Management, and Information Retrieval Journal). Please refer to his university webpage and Google Scholar profile for further details. He has played an active role in co-organizing multiple conferences (SIGIR-AP 2024, Australasian Database Conference 2024), workshops (R\(^3\)AG at SIGIR-AP 2024 and SIGIR-AP 2025, EReL@MIR at The Web Conference 2025, AISTORY at ICCV 2025 and CVPR 2026), and evaluation tasks (Temporalia at NTCIR-11 and NTCIR-12, AKG at at NTCIR-13 and FEHU at NTCIR-19).

docs.title: Open Intern Positions
docs.text:
In our lab, there are always open intern positions for outstanding and highly motivated undergraduate/mater/Ph.D students. The research topics include, but not limited to, information retrieval, machine learning, data analysis, etc.

The compensation is determined according to the regulations of University of Tsukuba.

Applicants are encouraged to assemble and submit the application package composed of CV, a 1-2 page summary of the past research accomplishments. Application package should be sent by e-mail to: yuhaitao@slis.tsukuba.ac.jp

docs.title: Two Open Postdoc Positions
docs.text:
We are seeking outstanding and highly motivated postdoctoral candidates to join the School of Informatics at University of Tsukuba, Japan.

Required Qualifications: . PhD (or close to completion of PhD) in Computer Science, Information Systems or a related area . Applications with research experience in data mining, text mining, artificial intelligence, or information retrieval are welcome . Strong publication record with publications in top level conferences and/or journals . Strong research skills . Strong programming skills . Strong verbal and written communication skills . Self-motivated with a strong work ethic and ability to work independently

The postdoctoral researcher will be working under the supervision of Dr. Haitao Yu as well as in collaboration with project collaborators: Professor Adam Jatowt. A particular advantage of the position is that it is a pure research position, with no need for administrative tasks like deliverable writing etc. The position is initially for one year, with the possibility of extension for additional 1-2 years upon mutual consent. Starting time should be from November/December, 2020 but this can be negotiable.

Applicants are encouraged to assemble and submit the application package composed of CV, a 1-2 page summary of the past research accomplishments, 1-2 representative publications and contact information for 1-2 reference providers. Application package should be sent by e-mail to: yuhaitao@slis.tsukuba.ac.jp

All applications arriving before November 1, 2020, will be given full consideration, but the call remains open until the position has been filled.

Regarding the salary, the basic information is shown below, for more details, please contact Haitao Yu via email.

This project (A Novel Interactive Information Retrieval System Using Deep Neural Network) is supported by the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS), 2017-04 -- 2019-03.

PI: Hai-Tao Yu.

The target of this research is to develop enhanced techniques to improve the user-experience when users are browsing, searching and retrieving desired information.

docs.title: Research Topics
docs.text:
I'd like to abstract my research as Information Intelligence, namely retrieving relevant information from large volumes of raw data and transforming them into useful knowledge and actionable intelligence. Here, the raw data can be text/image on the web, search log, collection of documents, data observed by robots, collection of recorded user behaviors, etc.

Towards efficient and effective Information Intelligence, the currently focused research topics can be listed as below:

  • Knowledge Graph
  • User Understanding
  • Commonsense Reasoning
  • Trustworthy Information Retrieval
  • Computational Human-value Understanding

docs.title: Trustworthy Information Retrieval
docs.text: IR systems play a remarkable role in bridging the ever-increasing world wide web with vast users’ information needs ranging from simply finding information to acquiring knowledge and making decisions. IR technologies, therefore, have a significant impact across many domains, such as digital libraries, e-commerce, news recommendation, healthcare search, patent search, job search, just to name a few. We aim to make an endeavor for achieving trustworthy IR technologies through exploring the following aspects:

docs.title: AI-powered Search
docs.text: Benefiting from the revolution of LLM and generative AI, AI-powered search systems can smoothly interact with users and automate many tasks, freeing people from the tedious process of searching, extracting and digesting information from multiple sources.

docs.title: Privacy-preserving Information Retrieval
docs.text: Modern IR systems can achieve enhanced performance by analyzing huge amounts of log data gathered from users. Unfortunately, the data to derive such insights is personal and sensitive, which might give rise to catastrophic consequences, even if the system collecting such data has resolved to ‘do no evil’. By now, accurately and efficiently providing satisfactory results to users while preserving privacy is far from being resolved. This research topic aims to initiate research into privacy-preserving IR and develop scalable privacy-preserving IR methods.

docs.title: Multimodal Information Retrieval
docs.text: Surpassing the constraints of data modality, Multimodal Information Retrieval integrates and aligns heterogeneous data sources (such as text, images, audio, and video) so as to enable more comprehensive and context-aware search experiences.

docs.title: Concersational Information Retrieval
docs.text: The technique of Concersational Information Retrieval allows user interaction and provides adaptive search results. Essentially it can be viewed as context-driven information retrieval, the context information includes previously submitted queries, interactive behaviors, etc. Fine-grained topics include user modeling, intent identification, behavior understanding, adaptive item ranking, etc.

docs.title: Retrieval-augmented Generation (RAG)
docs.text: Benefiting from the boom of deep learning and the recent success of LLMs, generative AI have taken the world by storm, posing a significant impact on the entire AI community. Unfortunately, LLMs are prone to hallucinations—producing inaccurate or fictitious content. To cope with this challenge, RAG has emerged as a promising paradigm for integrating information retrieval methods to improve the output of LLMs.

docs.title: Design of Evaluation Metric/Method
docs.text: Benefiting from the boom of deep learning and the recent success of LLMs, the generative AI revolution is reshaping the landscape of IR, powering technologies from traditional 10-blue-links retrieval to AI-powered search. Given the advanced IR technologies, how to effectively evaluate the performance becomes a pressing challenge.

docs.title: Commonsense Reasoning
docs.text: According to the Oxford English Dictionary, common sense is described as: ``Intelligence or sagacity in relation to practical matters arising in everyday life; the ability to make sound judgments and sensible decisions regarding such matters''. The commonsense knowledge about general concepts and activities is trivial for humans, yet is surprisingly difficult to acquire by AI systems. In order to develop AI systems that can perform human-like natural communication and reasoning, the so-called commonsense intelligence becomes the fundamental challenge. We aim to make an endeavor for endowing AI systems with commonsense intelligence through exploring the following aspects:

docs.title: Multimodal Generative Commonsense Reasoning
docs.text: The ability of generative commonsense reasoning (GCR) reflects how well an AI system can produce trustworthy outputs that align with real-world commonsense knowledge. By multimodal, we aim to surpassing the constraints of data modality so as to achieve more comprehensive and context-aware GCR.

docs.title: User Modeling
docs.text: Nowadays, enormous volume of search requests are submitted everyday. For example, Google processes over 3.5 billion searches per day (according to Internet Live Stats). Query logs capture and store interactions between search engines and their users and comprise a source of rich information regarding the ways in which users express their information needs, seek and select desired information units. This technique aims to extract the knowledge embedded in query logs in order to understand users, facilitate research of relevant fields, such as Information Retrieval and Recommender Systems.

docs.title: Knowledge Graph
docs.text: Knowledge Graph is a structured representation of knowledge in a graph format. For example, A triple-based Knowledge Graph consists of entities, concepts, and their relationships, where nodes denote entities (such as individuals, locations, or objects), and edges define semantic relationships between them. docs.title: Computational Human-value Understanding
docs.text: The recent advancements in LLMs have significantly revolutionized AI-oriented applications across various domains. However, alongside advanced AI capabilities come potential harmful impacts on individuals and societies that we are not yet fully prepared to handle well. We aim to cope with the potential harmful impacts of LLM-driven AI systems (LLMAISs) through the lens of computational human-value understanding. The core principle is: Real-world human-centric activities are driven by human values. If LLMAISs can fully understand the nuances of real-world human values, and align their behaviors with our desired human values, humanity can expect to live in harmony with AI systems.
